html:
A financial panic that began in London in June 1772 and spread to Scotland, Amsterdam and beyond.

It started when the banker Alexander Fordyce fled after heavy losses on speculation in East India Company shares, and his bank collapsed. Other banks that had lent to each other fell with it. In Scotland the Ayr Bank, which had lent recklessly, failed. The Bank of England stepped in to support sound firms. Panic reached Amsterdam, where the house of Clifford failed, and credit froze for months.

The crisis hurt the East India Company, which asked parliament for a loan. The Tea Act of 1773, meant to help it sell tea in America, led to the Boston Tea Party.

The historian Fernand Braudel saw a deeper meaning. London recovered quickly, while Amsterdam was badly shaken. To him this showed that the centre of the world economy was passing to London.
sum: A financial panic that began in London in June 1772 and spread to Scotland, Amsterdam and beyond.
